name: Mount Everest (Chomolungma / Sagarmatha)
blurb: The summit of Everest is the highest point on Earth measured from sea level. Its exact height was revised to 8,849 m in 2020 when Nepal and China jointly re-surveyed it with snow-cap included.

record: Tallest mountain from base to summit
name: Mauna Kea
value: 10,210 m (33,500 ft) from the ocean floor
blurb: Measured from its base on the Pacific sea floor, the dormant volcano Mauna Kea is taller than Everest — though only 4,207 m of it rise above sea level.

name: Ojos del Salado
blurb: The highest volcano on Earth, and the highest peak outside Asia. It last erupted a few centuries ago and hosts the world's highest known lake, a tiny crater pond near 6,390 m.

name: Mount Everest
blurb: Topographic prominence measures how far a summit stands above the lowest saddle linking it to any higher peak. No mountain on Earth is more isolated-and-dominant than Everest — its prominence equals its height.

name: Nile
blurb: The north-flowing Nile has watered Egyptian civilisation for millennia. Measuring rivers depends on which tributary counts as the source, so the Amazon is a close rival — but the Nile is the most widely accepted answer.

name: Amazon
blurb: The Amazon discharges more water than the next seven largest rivers combined — around one fifth of all river water reaching the ocean. Its estuary is so wide the sea turns fresh for tens of kilometres.

name: Congo River
blurb: Cutting through gorges as it crosses the rift, the Congo reaches soundings deeper than most harbours — deep enough that the river never freezes and ships ride a steady, dark swell.

name: Grand Canal of China
blurb: Built and rebuilt from the 5th century BC onward, the Grand Canal is the longest and oldest canal still in use — a continuous waterway that bound the rice-rich south to the capital in the north.

name: Caspian Sea
blurb: Landlocked and saline, the Caspian is classed as the world's largest enclosed inland body of water — big enough to be called a sea, yet bordered entirely by coastline with no outlet to the ocean.

name: Lake Superior
blurb: The biggest of North America's Great Lakes holds enough fresh water to carpet the whole of the Americas an inch deep. Its own cold moderates the surrounding climate like a small inland sea.

name: Lake Baikal
value: 1,642 m (5,386 ft) deep; ~25 million years old
blurb: Baikal is both the deepest lake and among the oldest on Earth, holding around a fifth of all unfrozen fresh surface water. Its age has produced hundreds of species found nowhere else.

name: Lake Titicaca
blurb: The world's highest commercially navigable lake, and the birthplace of the Inca creation myth. Its deep, cold water moderates the altiplano climate around it.

name: Lake Tanganyika
blurb: The longest and second-deepest lake in the world, Tanganyika is a narrow, trench-like rift lake that home to a rich trove of cichlid fish found only here.

name: Pacific Ocean
value: about 165 million km² (64 million sq mi)
blurb: Larger than all the Earth's land combined, the Pacific spans more than a third of the planet's surface and ringed by the volatile 'Ring of Fire' of trenches and volcanoes.

record: Deepest known point in the ocean
name: Challenger Deep, Mariana Trench
blurb: So deep that Mount Everest, dropped in, would be drowned by over two kilometres of water. Only a handful of crewed dives have ever reached its floor, where life still thrives in the black.

name: Arctic Ocean
value: about 15.6 million km² (6 million sq mi)
blurb: The Arctic is the ocean the size of a continent and the shallowest of them all, capped much of the year by drifting sea ice that has been thinning rapidly in recent decades.

name: Bay of Fundy
blurb: The funnel shape of the Bay of Fundy amplifies the Atlantic tide so that billions of tonnes of water surge in and out twice a day — exposing the world's highest coastal mudflats.

name: Angel Falls (Salto Ángel)
blurb: The water falls so far from Auyantepui that much of it turns to mist before reaching the ground. Named for pilot Jimmie Angel, who first flew over it in 1937.

name: Victoria Falls (Mosi-oa-Tunya)
blurb: Called 'the smoke that thunders', Victoria presents the largest unbroken curtain of falling water on Earth, its spray visible from dozens of kilometres away.

name: Mammoth Cave
blurb: The longest known cave on the planet, still being extended by survey each year — enough passages to bury a city, formed over millions of years as water dissolved limestone beneath the plateau.

name: Veryovkina Cave
blurb: Reaching the bottom of Veryovkina takes explorers several days straight down through shafts, sumps and rivers — deeper than any mountain is high.

name: Hang Sơn Đoòng
blurb: The largest cave passage in the world by volume — big enough to hold a jungle, its own weather and dolines where clouds drift in through collapsed ceilings.

name: Kali Gandaki Gorge
value: about 1,450 m (4,760 ft) from river to peaks
blurb: Carved by the Kali Gandaki where it threads between two of the world's highest mountains, this is measured as the deepest cut any river has made through the land surface.

name: Grand Canyon
blurb: The Colorado River exposed nearly two billion years of Earth history in its walls. Its scale — length, depth and breadth together — makes it the classic 'largest' canyon, though not the single-deepest.

name: Sahara
value: about 9.2 million km² (3.6 million sq mi)
blurb: Nearly the size of the United States, the Sahara is the world's largest hot desert — a shifting mosaic of sand seas, gravel plains and rock plateaus that was green with lakes a few thousand years ago.

name: Antarctic Desert
value: about 14.2 million km² (5.5 million sq mi)
blurb: By the scientific definition — low precipitation — the biggest desert on Earth is the frozen continent of Antarctica, where almost nothing falls as snow and the interior is a polar hyper-arid wasteland.

name: Atacama Desert
value: some weather stations with no rain on record
blurb: The driest desert on Earth outside the poles; parts of the Atacama have never had a recorded rainfall. Its soils resemble Mars, which is why robot rovers are tested here.

name: Antarctic Ice Sheet
value: about 14 million km², up to 4.8 km thick
blurb: Holding around 60 percent of all the fresh water on Earth locked as ice, the Antarctic sheet presses the continent down and drives the planet's ocean circulation.

name: Vostok Station
blurb: The lowest reliably measured air temperature anywhere on the planet, recorded at the Russian Vostok research station on the polar plateau in mid-winter.

name: Lambert Glacier
blurb: The widest and among the longest glaciers on Earth, the Lambert drains an area of ice the size of Western Europe, flowing several metres a day toward the sea.

name: Greenland
blurb: The world's biggest island (Australia is classed as a continent). About four fifths of Greenland is buried under a permanent ice sheet, so most people live on the ice-free coast.

name: Great Barrier Reef
blurb: The biggest living structure on the planet, built by billions of coral polyps and visible from space. It shelters an extraordinary array of fish, turtles and molluscs.

name: Canada
blurb: Canada has by far the longest shoreline of any country — more than the next several nations combined — fringed by three oceans and thousands of islands.

name: Burj Khalifa
blurb: The tallest human-made structure ever built, its observation deck at 555 m is the world's highest. Completed in 2010, it more than doubled the record height set only decades earlier.

name: Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge
blurb: A railway viaduct longer than the distance across many countries end to end, carrying the Beijing–Shanghai high-speed line across rice paddies, canals and the edge of Yangcheng Lake.

name: Gotthard Base Tunnel
blurb: The world's longest and deepest rail link, boring straight through the Alps between Zurich and Milan at over 2,300 m depth — twenty years in the making, opened in 2016.

name: Lærdal Tunnel
blurb: The longest road tunnel on Earth, with lit 'golden hour' caverns placed at intervals to give drivers rest and to fight fatigue on the single bore through the mountains.

record: Highest bridge deck above a valley
name: Beipanjiang (Duge) Bridge
blurb: The tallest bridge in the world by deck height, its road spans a canyon more than half a kilometre above the Beipan River — higher than the Eiffel Tower could stand beneath it.

name: 1915 Çanakkale Bridge
blurb: The longest central span of any suspension bridge ever built, opening in 2022 to leap the Dardanelles and end a ferry crossing that has been famous since antiquity.

name: Great Wall of China
blurb: Not one wall but many, built and rebuilt over two thousand years. A comprehensive archaeological survey measures every branch and ruin at nearly 21,000 km — roughly half way around the globe.

name: Statue of Unity
blurb: The tallest statue in the world, depicting independence leader Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. It dwarfs the previous record-holder, China's Spring Temple Buddha, by over a hundred metres.

name: Rungrado 1st of May Stadium
blurb: The biggest sports venue on Earth. Its flower-petal roof and 80,000-plus seat bowl are used for the country's mass games as well as football.

name: Arsenalna Station
blurb: Trains here descend on the world's longest escalators, over two minutes of travel down to reach the platform beneath a steep ravine on the right bank of the Dnipro.

name: King Fahd International Airport
blurb: The largest airport site in the world, its grounds bigger than the city of Dammam it serves — a planned city of runways, cargo and future development in the desert.

name: El Alto International Airport
blurb: The highest airport in the world that handles scheduled jet airliners. Thin high-altitude air lengthens take-off rolls and limits how much payload planes can carry.

name: Death Valley (Furnace Creek)
blurb: Among the highest air temperatures ever reliably recorded, in one of the hottest places on Earth — a below-sea-level basin where the sun, ground and dry air all conspire.

name: Mawsynram
blurb: This village in northeast India averages the highest rainfall ever measured for a settled place — the monsoon funnels up the bay of Bengal and is wrung out against the hills.

name: Barrow Island (Cyclone Olivia)
blurb: The strongest surface wind gust ever reliably recorded — faster than the terminal velocity of a skydiver — measured by an automatic station as Cyclone Olivia passed.

name: Oymyakon
blurb: A village that stays populated through winters colder than anywhere else on Earth, where thermometers have dipped near −70 °C and fuel, engines and eyelashes all freeze.
